primary_diagnosis: Undiagnosed / poorly-controlled Diabetes Mellitus (with or without diabetic kidney disease)
clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient is a 70‑year‑old Black female with stage‑4 CKD, severe hypercholesterolaemia, marked proteinuria, and ketonuria. These findings, together with hypertension and high cardiovascular risk, point most strongly toward undiagnosed diabetes mellitus as the primary driver of renal disease and dyslipidaemia. Primary glomerular disease and hypertensive nephrosclerosis are the next most plausible renal etiologies, while secondary hyperlipidaemia (nephrotic or hypothyroid) and silent coronary artery disease explain the lipid profile and overall risk. Remaining diagnoses address less likely but possible contributors (cardiorenal syndrome, CKD‑MBD, renal artery stenosis, drug‑induced nephritis, autoimmune vasculitis, obstruction, plasma‑cell dyscrasia).
unresolved_findings: Urine ketones (7.7 mg/dL) – unexplained without confirmed diabetes or fasting
Platelet count high‑normal (399.6 ×10³/µL) – reactive but no clear inflammatory trigger
Serum chloride 107.9 mmol/L (borderline high) – no clear acid‑base correlate
Serum CO₂ 22.1 mmol/L (low‑normal) – mild metabolic acidosis, could be CKD‑related
Serum calcium 10.2 mg/dL (upper‑normal) – may herald secondary hyperparathyroidism
Total bilirubin 0.4 mg/dL noted as rising – no hepatic source identified
recommended_workup: Fasting plasma glucose and HbA1c to confirm or exclude diabetes mellitus
Quantitative proteinuria assessment (spot urine albumin‑to‑creatinine ratio or 24‑hour urine protein) and serum albumin
Comprehensive lipid panel with apolipoprotein B and repeat LDL‑C after fasting
Thyroid function tests (TSH, free T4, anti‑TPO antibodies) to evaluate secondary hyperlipidaemia
Blood pressure trend review (clinic logs, home/ambulatory monitoring)
Full medication reconciliation focusing on NSAIDs, PPIs, antibiotics, and other nephrotoxins
Cardiac evaluation: BNP/NT‑proBNP, transthoracic echocardiogram, and coronary artery calcium scoring or stress testing
Renal imaging: ultrasound with Doppler to assess kidney size, echogenicity, hydronephrosis, and renal artery flow
Autoimmune serology (ANA, anti‑dsDNA, complement C3/C4, ANCA) for lupus or vasculitis
Bone‑mineral panel (intact PTH, phosphate, 25‑OH vitamin D, alkaline phosphatase) for CKD‑MBD
Serum free light chain assay and urine immunofixation to screen for multiple myeloma
Repeat complete blood count with differential to monitor for anemia or leukocytosis
